subject: RFI: model change-control assurances and open-model licensing details
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acmetech.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmetech.com
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: model change-control + licensing questions

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Acme's security and procurement teams are consolidating RFI answers for our vendor selection. Attached is a short questionnaire focused on model licensing, provenance, and update controls. High-level asks we need answered by next Friday:

1) For open-source models you serve, what licensing obligations do your customers inherit? Do you provide a mapping of included model components and their licenses?
2) Describe how you record model provenance (origin, training data markers, checkpoints) and how customers can verify pinned versions.
3) When a model update is available (security patch, new weights, or behavior change), how are customers notified and how can they opt into or block automatic updates?
4) Do you provide a signed attestation that no restricted third-party components were added in a given catalog export?
5) Please include a machine-readable export of the model catalog for our asset inventory.

We appreciate concise answers and any attachments (attestations, catalog CSV, sample manifest). If we can get a draft by next Thursday we can circulate it internally.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Li
Vendor Risk Manager, Acme Technology
security@acmetech.com

Attachment: acme_rfi_questions_model_licensing.docx
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acmetech.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 10:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: model change-control + licensing questions

Hi Sarah — thanks for sending. We're happy to respond and have started a short bundle that addresses each ask. High-level bullets below; attached is a draft PDF with more detail and a CSV export of the current model catalog. We'll finalize a signed attestation once legal signs off (looping internal counsel).

Quick answers:
- Licensing inheritance: For open models we surface the model's license on each catalog entry (e.g., Apache-2.0, MIT, CC-BY-4.0). Customers inherit the model's upstream license obligations; where special redistribution clauses apply we note them in the catalog entry and in the RFI bundle.
- Provenance: Each catalog entry includes upstream source URL, upstream commit/tag (when available), model hash (SHA256 of the checkpoint), and a collection timestamp. We also maintain an internal chain-of-custody log for onboarding events (who validated, when).
- Version pinning & updates: Customers may pin a specific model version ID in their config. By default hosted routes use a pinned stable variant; we only auto-upgrade if customers opt into 'auto-update' in their deployment policy. Update notifications are sent via email and the Console (and we publish a changelog and security bulletins).
- Attestation: We can provide a per-export signed attestation confirming the catalog snapshot and that no restricted third-party binaries were injected after ingestion.
- Catalog export: attached CSV; manifest includes license and provenance fields.

I'll attach the draft RFI bundle (RFI_Answers_Model_Change_Control.pdf) and catalog export for your inventory team. Expect a final attestation (signed PDF) by next Thursday pending legal review.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai

Attachments: RFI_Answers_Model_Change_Control.pdf, model-catalog-export-20270302.csv
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 08:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: draft RFI answers — legal/redline request

Rachel — forwarding the draft you circulated. A few redlines from compliance/legal I recommend before we sign:

- Attestation language: change 'no restricted third-party binaries' to 'no known restricted third-party binaries as of snapshot timestamp' to limit retrospective claims.
- Clarify license mapping: add explicit statement that we do not relicense upstream models and customers remain responsible for adherence to upstream license terms.
- Add retention window: specify how long we keep provenance metadata (we have it for minimum 3 years by default).

I've annotated RFI_Answers_Model_Change_Control.pdf (see comments) and exported a fresh model-catalog-export-20270303.csv with the extra license_column. Marcus — can you confirm the SHA256 hash field is included in the export?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Principal Compliance Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachment: model-catalog-export-20270303.csv
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 11:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: draft RFI answers — legal/redline request

All — confirmed, the catalog export includes: upstream_source, upstream_commit, license, sha256_checkpoint, ingest_timestamp, model_variant_id. I agree with Neha's wording tweaks; small note on pinning copy — recommend: 'Customers can pin by model_variant_id; pinned assets remain immutable until changed by customer action or a signed migration process'.

I've added a short playbook blurb for commands we give customers to export a pinned manifest from the console (two-line CLI snippet). Once legal okays the attestation wording we can sign and send back.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acmetech.com>, procurement@acmetech.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Final: RFI responses + signed attestation and catalog export

Hi Sarah — apologies for the delay and thanks for the patience. Attached are the finalized items we discussed:

1) RFI_Answers_Model_Change_Control.pdf — concise Q&A covering licensing, provenance, pinning, and update controls (incorporates legal redlines).
2) Licensing_Attestation_signed.pdf — per-export signed attestation (signed by our General Counsel) confirming the catalog snapshot timestamp and that no known restricted third-party binaries were added post-ingest.
3) model-catalog-export-20270308.csv — machine-readable export suitable for inventory ingestion. It includes license, upstream source, upstream commit, sha256 hash, and variant IDs.

Key operational notes for Acme:
- Pinning: To pin, use the Console or API to set model_variant_id on your deployment. Pinned models are immutable from our side; we will not auto-upgrade pinned models unless you change the flag.
- Updates: We publish security bulletins and a changelog. If you opt into 'managed-updates' we will schedule coordinated upgrades with a rollback window.
- Attestation frequency: we can provide a signed attestation per catalog snapshot on a monthly or per-request cadence; let me know which you prefer.

I've included links to a one-page runbook and a DocuSign copy of the attestation (https://docusign.example.com/3f4b2c-attestation). Please confirm receipt and whether Acme would like monthly snapshots or per-request attestations. Happy to jump on a call if you want to walk through the pinning workflow.

Best regards,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: RFI_Answers_Model_Change_Control.pdf, Licensing_Attestation_signed.pdf, model-catalog-export-20270308.csv
